overview.description: Five Hundred is a trick-taking game for four players in fixed partnerships, invented in the USA in 1904 and now the national card game of Australia. Players bid 6-10 tricks; the high bidder takes a 3-card kitty, discards 3 cards, declares trump, and attempts to win their bid. Features unique bower mechanics (Joker and jacks of matching suit as top trumps) and No Trump / Misere contract options. First partnership to reach 500+ points wins.
overview.origin: USA (1904), popularized in Australia & New Zealand

history.origins: Five Hundred was invented in the USA in 1904 by the U.S. Playing Card Company, copyrighted officially in 1904. It evolved from Euchre, adding a 43-card pack (stripping 2s-6s) and a Joker, plus a bidding system for tricks and the 'kitty' (widow) mechanism.
timeline: 1904: Invented and trademarked by US Playing Card Company; rules published.
1920s-1950s: Becomes the national game of Australia; also popular in New Zealand and parts of North America.
1960s-1980s: Peak popularity in Oceania; spreads to South Africa.
Present: Remains the national game of Australia; played competitively worldwide.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Euchre by introducing: (1) variable hand bidding (6-10 tricks), (2) the kitty/widow mechanic, (3) No Trump and Misere contracts, (4) scoring points toward a fixed target (500 points).
history.cultural: Five Hundred holds a unique cultural position as the official national card game of Australia. In Australian clubs and homes, it is played with intense competitiveness and strategic depth. The game embodies values of partnership cooperation and calculated risk.

setup.players: Exactly 4 players in 2 fixed partnerships (seated opposite each other).
setup.deck: 43-card deck: Remove all 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s, 6s from a standard 52-card deck, keeping 7-A in all suits. Add 1 Joker. Total: 43 cards + 1 Joker = 44 cards.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and right-hand player cuts. Dealer distributes: 3 cards to each player, then 3 cards to the kitty (widow), then 4 more cards to each player. Final distribution: each player holds 10 cards; 3-card kitty placed in center.

rules.objective: First partnership to score 500+ points wins the game. Points are earned by making bid contracts.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding Phase**: Starting with player left of dealer, each player bids the number of tricks they believe they can win (6-10) and optionally names trump or passes. Bids increase; last bid stands (highest wins). Player may bid only once. 2. **Kitty Discovery**: Winning bidder takes the 3-card kitty, examines it, and discards 3 cards face-down (kitty discards are never revealed). 3. **Trump Declaration**: High bidder announces trump suit OR 'No Trumps' (or 'Misere' / 'Open Misere' if their contract value supports it). 4. **Play Phase**: High bidder leads the first trick. Each player must follow suit if able. Trick won by highest trump or highest card of led suit. Trick winner leads next. 5. **Scoring**: After all 10 tricks, count tricks won by high bidder's partnership. If bid made: partners score the contract points. If failed: partners score negative points; opponents score 10 per trick won. 6. **Next Deal**: Deal passes left after each hand.
keyRules: **Card Rankings**: In trump suit: Joker (highest) > Right Bower (jack of trump) > Left Bower (jack of same color) > A > K > Q > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7. Non-trump: A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7.
**Bowers**: The jack of trump suit (Right Bower) and the jack of the same color as trump (Left Bower) are the two highest-ranking cards in trump.
**No Trumps**: All suits rank normally (A-K-Q-J-10...7). Joker is a nominate card (player specifies which suit it belongs to before play) or unsuit card (playable only when void in led suit).
**Misere**: Contractor must lose all 10 tricks. Partners never score points; only contractors lose (if successful, they score 250 points; if failed, negative points). Joker and bowers irrelevant.
**Open Misere**: Misere with contractor's hand exposed after first trick. Scores 500 points if successful.
**Trick Management**: Must follow suit if able; otherwise, any card may be played. No forced trump.
**Kitty Discard**: High bidder's three discarded cards are never revealed and are not counted in scoring.

strategy.basic: In the kitty, seek cards that complement your hand (completing suits or adding bowers). Bid conservatively early; trust your partner's bids. Always follow suit. If high bidder, play trump cards to establish who holds what.
strategy.intermediate: **Bid Calculation**: Count sure tricks + tricks your partner likely has from their bid signals. A 6-trick bid requires only 6/10 tricks (60% win rate); 10-trick requires 10/10 (100%). **Bower Recognition**: If you hold Left Bower, remember Right Bower is still higher in trump. **No Trump Strategy**: Be cautious; without trump, your Ace is no longer highestâ€”opponents' cards block you easily.
strategy.advanced: **Bid Communication**: Your bid signals your hand strength. Conservative bids suggest weak hands; aggressive bids suggest strong trump holdings. Partners interpret bids to guide their play. **Counting Out**: Track which high cards have been played to calculate remaining trick probabilities. **Misere Play**: Requires exceptional discipline. Avoid taking any tricks and don't play bower cards.
tips: Early in a bid, save low trump cards (7s, 8s) for later tricks when bowers are exhausted.
If partner bids 8, they likely hold strong trump. Don't compete unless you also have exceptional trump length.
In No Trump, Aces are valuable but not invincible. Track where high cards land.
Always communicate through your bid. Overbidding signals strength; underbidding signals weakness.

difficulty.easy: Bids conservatively (always 6 tricks if possible). Plays top cards first; doesn't track cards. Ignores partner signals.
difficulty.medium: Bids based on hand strength (6-7 tricks with weak hand, 8-9 with strong). Follows suit correctly. Understands bowers. Tracks obvious cards.
difficulty.hard: Sophisticated bidding using hand strength + probability models. Counts all played cards perfectly. Models partner hand from bid and play. Calculates exact trick probabilities. Uses psychology to signal strength and extract information from opponents' bids and plays.

considerations: AI must understand Bower mechanics: Right Bower > Left Bower in trump suit.
AI must model partner communication through bids and card play.
AI must calculate trick probabilities based on remaining card distribution.
AI must understand No Trump trump suits: Joker requires pre-announcement.
AI must recognize when to bid Misere (very weak hand) vs standard contracts.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit if able. Otherwise, any card. Joker in No Trumps subject to nomination rules.

discard.description: Choose 3 cards from hand to discard face-down (never revealed).
discard.constraints: High bidder only. Must discard exactly 3 after taking kitty.

pass.description: Decline to bid. Player is out of the bidding for this hand.
pass.constraints: May pass on first turn or after hearing a higher bid.

bid.description: Bid the number of tricks (6-10) you believe your partnership will win. Optionally name trump or pass to No Trump declaration.
bid.constraints: Bid must be higher than previous highest bid. Once a player passes, they cannot rebid.

go_out.reason: Game has no going out mechanic.

engine.deckDescription: A 32-card deck formed by removing all ranks 2 through 6 from a standard pack, leaving 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace in each of four French suits.
engine.suitDescription: French suits: hearts (cœurs), diamonds (carreaux), clubs (trèfles), and spades (piques). Each suit has eight cards in the 32-card pack.
engine.rankDescription: Stripped 32-card ranking: each suit has eight cards from 7 (low) up through 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, and Ace high.
engine.dealPattern: 3 to each player and kitty, 4 to each player

synthesis.shortDescription: An Euchre variant played by four players in partnerships with bidding, a kitty (widow), variable trump declaration, and sophisticated scoring.

prompts.human: Welcome to Five Hundred, the national game of Australia. You play in partnerships. Bid the tricks you can win. If high bidder, take the kitty and declare trump. Make your bid and score points toward 500. Work with your partnerâ€”your bids communicate your hand strength.

scoring.description: Scoring based on contract value and tricks won. First partnership to 500+ points wins.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach 500 or more cumulative points wins the game.

penalties.Failed Bid: Contractor's partnership scores negative contract value. Opponents score 10 points per trick won.
penalties.Backward Line: A partnership reaching -500 points loses immediately.

scoring.splitRules: Contractor's partnership scores if bid is made (contract value). Opponents never score on contractor's failed bid, but always score 10 per trick won. In Misere/Open Misere: contractors score only if successful (250/500); opponents score zero.
